items.title: Build the id set of a repeated PromQL selector once per query
items.head: 15ec8bc23e76a041e889809cfebe48c3dfe3450a
items.claim: A repeated one-series selector builds its id set once. Measured run 1 (64-vCPU host, 16 pinned cores): about 6 ms off each repeat (x + x 41.6 -> 35.4 ms, -15%; x + x + x 59.1 -> 48.6 ms, -18%; ~200-series y + y -12%). A hit skips only the tags lookup's execution; the subquery is still planned and the samples are still read per selector. Single-use and offset controls unchanged.
items.pass_if: 05481 prints 1, 1, 2, 2 (and only those four rows); the repeated-selector queries of promql_repeated_selector.xml are significantly faster by at least 4 ms per repeat; no control or guard query is reported slower (rerun promql_selector_pk_range to settle the +1.1-1.8% seen in run 1).
items.notes: Run 1 failed the old 8 ms/repeat floor: that floor came from my 12-14 ms prediction, which wrongly counted per-query overhead as lookup cost; the 6 ms saved matches the lookup-only cost. Commit 15ec8bc fixes the 05481 log_comment filter (test-only; C++ unchanged). Decide: submit at ~6 ms/repeat (my recommendation: yes) or tell me drop. gtests PreparedSetsCache.* need ENABLE_TESTS=ON (or upstream CI). Related upstream: 118801 (broader, MaterializedCTE).

items.title: PromQL: skip the duplicate series check when dropping the metric name of one metric
items.head: dadc843ffb7478938ad1712ee757df247f78d093
items.claim: At 100k series: sum(rate) -19% CPU, sum(abs) -20%, sum by (job) -9%, a 37-step range query -30%, with identical results. The regex-selector control is unchanged.
items.pass_if: 05482 passes; the sum(rate), sum(abs) and range queries are faster by at least 10%; the regex control is not slower.
items.notes: Overlaps upstream 121069 (the same rule, range functions only) and James's own 126763: land only one of them. Decide before submitting. The last 2 reference lines of 05482 were predicted (one less than master prints): check them first.

items.title: Do not filter every row of the TimeSeries time ranges table by the id ranges of the selected metrics
items.head: c4af28626b55e50470733ce2a23754aaadb384d5
items.claim: Built (2026-11-01): 100-name alternation 176 -> 141 ms (-19.9%) in the in-tree perf test; 50-300 names of 500 series -35 to -39%. Controls and guards not slower.
items.pass_if: 05479 passes (prints 1 2); the 100-name alternation is faster by at least 25%; no control or guard query is reported slower.
items.notes: Judged a pass 2026-11-03 though the 25% floor was missed on the original table (-19.9%; -35 to -39% at 50-300 names of 500 series); the floor came from an over-optimistic emulation. Optional before submit: a read_rows assertion in 05479 that pins primary-key pruning (code change, would need another build). Upstream now has unrelated 05479_* tests; renumber only if the check asks.

items.title: Grow the timeSeries*ToGrid bucket map before a colliding wrapping index
items.head: 46291048116bdeeacd63aac63df0da25d4b5466d
items.claim: The gap and late-start cases lose their slowdown against the contiguous case (6.1x timeSeriesLastToGrid, 4.1x timeSeriesRateToGrid on master) and run about as fast as it. The contiguous case is unchanged.
items.pass_if: 05474 passes; the gap queries are at least 3x faster; the contiguous queries are not slower.
items.notes: Closes upstream issue 125759. Related upstream: 124773 (caused it), 124777.

items.title: Stop evaluating an ALP parameter pair once it cannot beat the best one
items.head: d4c58e0009b46e9e99a7eff37103452154534a4b
items.claim: ALP encode CPU -40-90% on decimal-like values and -2-9% on full-precision ones; compressed bytes identical.
items.pass_if: 05480 passes with its exact sizes; the 04612 and 05054 tests pass unchanged; codecs_float_alp_small_blocks INSERTs are faster; no codecs_float_insert query is reported slower.
items.notes: ALP is a beta codec behind enable_alp_codec; codec owners should review.
